ukraine-talks.title: Ending the war in Ukraine
ukraine-talks.intro: Russia's full-scale invasion is nearing its fifth year. The US is trying to broker a deal, while Kyiv worries Washington is stepping back from its support.

image.alt: Independence Square in central Kyiv on a grey day

events.text: Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The last round of US-mediated Russia–Ukraine talks takes place, days before the US–Israeli war on Iran begins.
US envoy Steve Witkoff meets Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
Ukraine accepts a US proposal for a three-way meeting of negotiators.
Witkoff meets Putin in St Petersburg, with Jared Kushner joining by video. Russia frees American Stephen Hubbard, and the Kremlin says talks could resume in mid-November, possibly in Abu Dhabi.
Overnight Russian missile strikes on Kyiv injure six people.
The toll from the overnight strikes on Kyiv rises to at least one dead and 22 injured, and Moscow says Ukraine sent 630 drones at the region.
Putin says Russia is ready to resume three-way talks, but on the terms of a final peace deal and not a short ceasefire.
Ukraine's defence minister says Starlink and Starshield connections are stable again after more than a week of restrictions.
Russia says it will open a humanitarian corridor to the occupied town of Oleshky, where residents are trapped by minefields, shelling and drones.
A local ceasefire around Oleshky takes effect ahead of a humanitarian mission the White House says was brokered by Melania Trump, while missile attacks resume on Kyiv.
The leaders of Finland and Norway hold a rare call with Putin, drawing criticism from Denmark.

iran-gulf.title: The Iran war and the Gulf
iran-gulf.intro: A US–Israeli war on Iran that began in February has spread across the region, disrupting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and drawing in Iran-aligned groups such as Yemen's Houthis.

image.alt: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula
image.credit: MODIS Land Rapid Response Team, NASA GSFC, public domain

events.text: The US and Israel launch a war on Iran.
Iran strikes targets across the region. Drones hit the US embassy in Riyadh.
The US and Iran reach a memorandum of understanding.
The US launches fresh strikes on Iran, and Iran says it has closed the Strait of Hormuz.
Saudi Arabia cancels its 'Davos in the Desert' conference because of Houthi strikes, and the US orders non-emergency staff to leave the kingdom.
An attack on King Fahd airport kills one person. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say their doctrine is now 'offensive', and Qatar and France call for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen.

A person briefed on war planning tells NPR the US and Israel are preparing for a possible attack on Iran in early November. Iranian state media says the IRGC targeted seven oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.
The death toll from the Houthi strike on King Fahd airport rises to two, and fighting intensifies in Yemen's Taiz, where the UN says nearly 260,000 people have been displaced since August.
Reports say the US and Israel are planning fresh strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections, and analysts warn emergency oil stocks are at multidecade lows.
Trump says the US 'may do another little Epic Fury' on Iran, and NPR reports military reinforcements moving to the Middle East.
Qatar's foreign minister says Iran must show good faith and reopen the Strait of Hormuz; another ship is struck in the Strait.
Egypt's parliament approves military support for Saudi Arabia if it is requested, as Houthi attacks threaten the kingdom.

france-unrest.title: Unrest in France
france-unrest.intro: Protests over the cost of living and fuel prices turned into some of France's worst street violence in years, shaking markets and politics.

image.alt: The Monument to the Republic on Place de la République in Paris

events.text: Protests in Paris against living costs and fuel prices turn violent.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu calls for curfews in cities hit by riots and looting.
Nightly curfews take effect in Paris, Bordeaux, Nice and other cities.
French bond yields rise above 5%, the highest since 2002, and police ban protests in parts of Paris for the next day.
The protest ban covers sites including the Élysée Palace, parliament, the Louvre and the Champs-Élysées from 8am to 8pm.
Macron says 'illegitimate' protests will be banned in the coming days, and the government says soldiers will be deployed on the streets.
Authorities say 70,000 security forces will be mobilised for Saturday protests, and Macron meets student representatives.
A second Saturday of protests passes under 70,000 police. The interior minister reports 135 arrests and no major incident so far.

ebola-2026.title: The 2026 Ebola outbreak
ebola-2026.intro: DR Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak on record is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, which has no approved vaccine, and it has now spread beyond the country.

image.alt: Electron micrograph of an Ebola virus particle

events.text: An Ebola outbreak begins in DR Congo. It has since recorded more than 9,000 cases and over 4,000 deaths.
A woman travels from Uganda to Abuja. She falls ill days later.
Kenya begins recording cases. Nine have been reported since.
Nigeria and the WHO confirm her case is the Bundibugyo strain. Officials trace 44 contacts.
The WHO warns Africa faces a 'complex' Ebola outbreak after the virus reaches Nigeria, the first case in the west of the continent.
Officials investigate whether the first Ebola patients in Nigeria and Kenya crossed paths at a Ugandan airport, and Kenya reports a second Ebola death.
Congo reports more than 10,000 Ebola cases and nearly 4,900 deaths, with no approved vaccine for the Bundibugyo virus.
Kenya has confirmed nine cases and released the first group of 20 contacts of its first patient; the European disease control centre sends experts to Nigeria.

sudan-war.title: Sudan's war
sudan-war.intro: Sudan's army and the paramilitary RSF have been fighting for control of the country since April 2023, and the UN warns the war is spilling over its borders.

image.alt: Khartoum at night, photographed from the International Space Station

events.text: War breaks out between Sudan's army and the Rapid Support Forces.
A drone strike hits the Amiet market in the Abyei area, which Sudan and South Sudan both claim. Local authorities blame the Sudanese army.
A local official says the death toll has reached 153 and is likely higher.
MSF says a Sudanese Armed Forces drone strike on a busy market in Nyala killed at least 36 people.
Western governments warn of a risk of famine as conflict, drought and funding cuts deepen the crisis.

israel-election.title: Israel's election
israel-election.intro: Israel held its first general election since the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023 on 27 October 2026, in a vote widely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

events.text: Hamas-led attacks on Israel trigger a chain of conflicts across the region.
Israelis vote in record numbers; turnout reaches about 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades.
Exit polls show opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's bloc narrowly ahead of Netanyahu's, 52 seats to 50, with Arab parties projected to win a combined 18 seats and no clear path to a government.

brazil-2026.title: Brazil's presidential election
brazil-2026.intro: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva beat Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in a close runoff on 25 October 2026, and the loser's refusal to concede has turned into a legal and diplomatic dispute.

events.text: Lula wins the runoff with 51.78% of valid votes to 48.22% for Flávio Bolsonaro; Bolsonaro says he will not recognise the result and will seek to annul the election.
The electoral court's president rejects Bolsonaro's case for annulment; Trump questions the result, while most Latin American governments congratulate Lula.
Bolsonaro's party acknowledges Lula's victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro does not concede; Brazil's Federal Police revoke his passports after he misses a deadline to hand them in.
Reports say Bolsonaro has left for the United States, and the US State Department says it will issue visas to him and his family.
